title: Dual Disruption in Ring Topology: Communication & Physical Decoupling
description: This scenario explores dual disruption dynamics within a ring communication topology. A relay loss for Agent A coincides with the closure of a critical physical bridge, testing the agents' ability to re-route freight and re-establish multi-hop communication paths under extreme constraints.
edge_cases_to_watch: Communication loss coincides with physical route closure
Agents cannot coordinate about the bridge closure due to Agent A's relay failure
Recovery requires handling both disruptions simultaneously
Information asymmetry: Agent B knows about the bridge, but cannot reach Agent A to warn them
Single-path bottlenecking: When the bridge closes, the remaining routes hit capacity limits
Multi-hop latency: Agents must use Agent C or D to relay messages to bypass the 'dead' node A
coordination_challenges: Information Propagation: Relay loss of Agent A forces all communication between B/C and D/A to use longer multi-hop paths.
Split-Brain Scenario: Agents on opposite sides of the ring may operate on outdated physical topology maps.
Congestion Cascades: Re-routing freight from the closed east-bridge onto the 'west-south' route causing capacity overflow.
Priority Conflict: Determining which agent takes the remaining capacity on the north-south route when high-priority jobs are delayed.
suggested_agent_strategies: Gossip-based Protocols: Agents should broadcast status updates to all neighbors to ensure info reaches the ring despite node loss.
Predictive Re-routing: Agents should preemptively move toward alternative depots when they detect a neighbor's silence.
Buffer Management: Holding low-priority freight at depots to reserve capacity for high-priority rerouted goods.
Redundancy: Using the 'west-bridge' as a secondary logical communication/transit corridor if the primary ring-path is saturated.

coordination_challenges: Communication loss coincides with physical route closure
Agents cannot coordinate about the bridge closure

success_criteria: Agents adapt communication to topology constraints
Recovery from disruption within expected turns
Zero capacity violations on remaining routes
